content.text: No arbitration provisions exist anywhere in the document; the clause matches the preferred position.

input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects New York law and Section 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, with each Party submitting to personal jurisdiction and waiving venue objections. That is exactly our preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York County courts). A document-wide search returns no arbitration provision, so there is no foreign seat or mandatory arbitration concern. The carve-out permitting either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere to protect confidential information or IP is mutual and customary, and the Section 28.3 executive escalation expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, so it does not impair our access to the courts. Compliant; no redline.
